title: Artichoke Music
venue_description:
Overview

Artichoke Music is a nonprofit community music center that has been at the heart of Portland's acoustic music scene since 1973. Named because artichokes are all heart the organization embodies its mission to make music accessible to everyone. This beloved venue serves as a music store performance space production studio and educational center all under one roof.

History and Mission

Founded by Judith Cook-Tucker in 1973 Artichoke Music has passed through the stewardship of several dedicated owners before Steve Einhorn took over in 1981. He and his wife Kate Power nurtured the venue into the wonderful community gathering place it is today. The organization is dedicated to building community through music by providing rewarding experiences for people of all ages to discover learn and play music.

Performance Venue

The intimate 50-person capacity listening room at Artichoke is considered one of Portland's finest acoustic venues. The space creates an atmosphere of reverence for music where audiences give performers their full attention. Live music happens Thursday through Sunday nights featuring a diverse range of acoustic genres including folk Americana blues jazz and singer-songwriter performances.

Open Mic and Jam Sessions

Artichoke hosts several regular open mic and jam sessions. The Acoustic Village Open Mic takes place every other Thursday providing a platform for musicians poets and storytellers. The Portland Bluegrass Sunday Jam occurs on the 2nd and 4th Sundays from 1:00 to 4:00 PM welcoming all skill levels for acoustic bluegrass jamming with a $5 cover at the door. Additional specialized events include Be Heard - An Open Mic for Women's Voices and the Free Open Mic for Teens and Young Adults.

Music Education

As an educational institution Artichoke offers music classes for various instruments and skill levels. Their teaching philosophy emphasizes creating a friendly encouraging environment where people feel welcomed and supported whether they've just picked up their first guitar or are ready to make music their profession. The organization also provides outreach to under-served communities expanding access to music education.

Community Impact

Artichoke Music is an integral part of the creative community of musicians in Portland and the Pacific Northwest. The venue has helped launch the careers of countless local musicians while fostering a connected community of acoustic music lovers. Their commitment to accessibility and community building has made them a cornerstone of Portland's music scene for over four decades.

title: Clyde's Prime Rib
venue_description:
Overview

Clyde's Prime Rib is a classic Portland restaurant that has become legendary in the city's jazz community. For over a decade this Northeast Portland establishment has been home to the Ron Steen Jazz Jam one of the most respected and longest-running jazz jam sessions in the Pacific Northwest.

Jazz Programming

Every Sunday night Clyde's hosts the Ron Steen Jazz Jam starting at 7:30 PM. Led by drummer Ron Steen - known as the Godfather of Jazz Jams in Portland - this session has been running continuously since the early 2000s. Ron Steen is a Portland Jazz Master member of the Oregon Music Hall of Fame and the Jazz Society of Oregon Hall of Fame and was named the 2020 Portland Jazz Hero by the Jazz Journalists Association.

Musical Excellence

The jam session attracts both established musicians and aspiring players creating an environment where younger artists can learn from experienced professionals. Notable international jazz stars who visit Portland often stop by Steen's jams for impromptu performances. The session operates on the principle of inclusivity providing a place for people to come and express themselves through music.

Atmosphere and Community

Clyde's provides a professional yet welcoming setting for jazz performance. The restaurant's commitment to hosting this weekly jam session demonstrates their dedication to supporting Portland's vibrant jazz community. The venue offers quality sound and an audience that appreciates and respects the art of jazz improvisation.

Legacy

Ron Steen has hosted ongoing jam sessions in Portland since 1980 and currently leads five different jam sessions throughout the week. His sessions are models of inclusivity and opportunities for musicians to test their skills connect with peers and carry on the jazz tradition. The Clyde's jam is a cornerstone of this legacy attracting musicians from across the region and beyond.

title: Wilf's Restaurant & Jazz Bar
venue_description:
Overview

Wilf's Restaurant & Jazz Bar is an elegant downtown Portland establishment that combines fine dining with exceptional live jazz music. Located in the heart of the city at 800 NW 6th Avenue Wilf's has established itself as one of Portland's premier jazz venues committed to supporting local artists and maintaining the highest standards of musical excellence.

Live Music Programming

Wilf's features live jazz music Wednesday through Saturday evenings with music starting at 7:00 PM. The venue has implemented an equity-based cover charge policy charging $5 per person which goes directly to the performing artists. This commitment ensures fair compensation for musicians and helps sustain Portland's vibrant jazz community. Most acts featured are local keeping the money in the area and supporting the lively arts scene.

Jazz Jam Sessions

Wednesday nights feature the Ron Steen Vocal Jazz Jam a specialized session focusing on vocal jazz and the Great American Songbook. Hosted by renowned drummer Ron Steen along with vocalists Lori Boone and Steve Christofferson this jam provides a rare opportunity for singers to perform with a professional rhythm section in an upscale setting. The session welcomes both experienced vocalists and those looking to develop their skills.

Venue Amenities

Wilf's offers both main dining room and bar seating with excellent sightlines to the stage. The restaurant features a top-of-the-line air filtration system ensuring a comfortable environment for diners and performers. Reservations are recommended especially for the best seating during live music nights. For those planning to leave before 7 PM no cover charge is required.

Dining Experience

As a full-service restaurant Wilf's offers a menu that complements the sophisticated jazz atmosphere. Guests can enjoy dinner drinks or both while experiencing some of the best jazz Portland has to offer. The venue strikes a perfect balance between fine dining and music venue creating an elegant yet accessible atmosphere.

COVID-19 Safety and Policies

Wilf's has maintained strict safety protocols including requiring reservations and ensuring all safety measures are met. Their commitment to community safety demonstrates their responsibility to staff customers and the broader Portland community.

title: Influence Music Hall
venue_description:
Overview

Influence Music Hall is a nonprofit community arts organization operated by Tualatin Valley Artists. Since 2006 this Hillsboro venue has been hosting Friday Night Open Mic one of the Portland area's longest-running and most beloved open mic events. The organization is dedicated to improving the community's quality of life by enhancing its art and culture.

Mission and Values

Influence Music Hall is focused on family-friendly community art and music with appreciative and supportive audiences. Their mission is to provide education quality gallery display poetry and musical performance all in an atmosphere of encouragement and opportunity. The venue operates as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization ensuring accessibility and community focus.

Friday Night Open Mic

Every Friday night from 7:00 PM until everyone has performed Influence Music Hall hosts an all-ages open mic event. Founded by Evan Acey the open mic has been running continuously for over 18 years. The format is simple: performers get 3 songs or 15 minutes whichever comes first. Sign-up starts at 6:30 PM with raffle tickets drawn at 7:00 PM to set the performance order. The hall stays open until everyone has had a chance to play.

Venue Facilities

The venue features a great sound system and house instruments including a grand piano guitars and full PA system. Free beer wine and snacks are provided to performers and audience members. The 1200 square foot space accommodates a wide variety of musical styles including rock jazz pop folk blues punk and more. The venue strictly enforces a no-talking policy during performances creating one of the most respectful listening environments in the region.

Art Gallery

In addition to music Influence Music Hall hosts the Hillsboro Art Walk displaying local artists' paintings drawings and photography throughout the space. This multi-disciplinary approach to the arts creates a rich cultural environment that celebrates all forms of creative expression.

Community Impact

Influence Music Hall has been described as a garden of fertile soil for emerging talent. Many musicians have sold CDs and landed paying gigs as a result of their performances at the hall. The venue provides opportunities ranging from light and sound engineering positions to regular performance slots at art walks. The supportive community atmosphere has helped launch numerous musical careers and fostered lasting connections between artists.

Location and Accessibility

The venue alternates between two Hillsboro locations: the Odd Fellows Hall at 267 E Main Street (odd months with elevator access for ADA compliance) and the Pythian Lodge at 151 SE 2nd Ave (even months). This rotating schedule keeps the experience fresh while maintaining the consistent quality and community spirit that defines Influence Music Hall.

title: Produce Row Café
venue_description:
Overview

Produce Row Café is a Portland institution that has been serving the community since 1974. Originally opened as a breakfast café for produce dockworkers in 1953 the venue was converted to a pub by Mike and Brian McMenamin in 1974 and has since become a beloved destination for craft beer enthusiasts and music lovers alike.

History and Evolution

The building was constructed in 1951 and has a rich history in Portland's industrial district. Before becoming Produce Row it served as both a breakfast café and a barbershop. The McMenamins transformed it into one of Portland's original craft beer bars helping to establish the city's reputation as a craft beer destination. The venue has evolved through multiple iterations from being the de facto home base of Portland's pre-millennial indie-rock crowd to an unlikely IDM and EDM hang in the 2000s before being revamped into a New Portland beer hall.

Music Programming

Produce Row has been home to multiple generations of Portland's music scene. The venue hosts a diverse range of live music events including the Tuesday night jazz jam session led by trumpet player Pablo Rivarola. The session begins at 8:00 PM with an hour of jazz from a rotating house band followed by two hours of curated jamming featuring some of Portland's best young jazz musicians. The venue also hosts funk nights DJ events and various other musical performances throughout the week.

Tuesday Jazz Jam

The Tuesday night jazz jam has become a cornerstone of Portland's jazz community. Led by Pablo Rivarola the session provides a platform for Portland's finest young jazz musicians to explore improvisation and connect with fellow players. The intimate basement-style venue creates a casual atmosphere perfect for musical experimentation and community building.

Beer and Food

Produce Row features an extensive craft beer selection with over 20 taps and more than 200 bottles showcasing local and international breweries. The venue offers two happy hours with separate menus (4-7 PM and 11 PM-2 AM) plus an all-day menu featuring American-style cuisine and comfort food. The covered and heated patio provides additional seating and has become a popular spot for outdoor gatherings.

Location and Atmosphere

Located in Portland's Central Eastside Industrial District at 204 SE Oak Street Produce Row is easily accessible with ample street parking. The venue maintains its Old Portland character while offering modern amenities. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming making it an ideal spot for gathering with friends seeing live music and everything in between. The venue's multiple spaces including the main room mural room and outdoor patio can accommodate events of various sizes.

title: Hopworks Urban Brewery
venue_description:
Overview

Hopworks Urban Brewery is a popular Southeast Portland brewery that combines award-winning organic craft beer with a strong commitment to sustainability and community engagement. Located at 2944 SE Powell Boulevard Hopworks has become a neighborhood gathering spot known for its welcoming atmosphere and support of local music.

Sustainability Mission

Hopworks is committed to sustainable brewing practices using organic ingredients and implementing environmentally friendly operations. This commitment extends to their food menu which features locally sourced ingredients whenever possible. The brewery's focus on sustainability has made them a leader in Portland's eco-conscious craft beer scene.

Bluegrass Jam Sessions

Every Thursday night Hopworks hosts a vintage bluegrass jam session led by Patrick and his rotating band. The jam celebrates classic bluegrass tunes from the 1940s 50s and 60s along with original songs in the same hard-driving traditional style. The sessions create a toe-tapping good time filled with lively music great vibes and cold drinks. Musicians and fans alike are welcome to join in the fun making it a true community event.

Taproom and Atmosphere

The brewery features a spacious taproom with both indoor and outdoor seating areas. The casual welcoming environment makes it perfect for enjoying live music while sampling their flagship brews seasonal offerings and limited releases. The venue provides a family-friendly atmosphere during earlier hours transitioning to a more adult-oriented vibe as the evening progresses.

Beer Selection

Hopworks offers an extensive lineup of organic beers including their flagship IPAs lagers and seasonal specialties. Their commitment to using organic ingredients sets them apart in Portland's competitive craft beer market. The brewery regularly rotates taps to feature new and experimental brews keeping the selection fresh and exciting for regular visitors.

Food Menu

The brewery serves a full menu featuring pizza burgers and vegetarian options. All items are made with care and attention to quality with an emphasis on local organic ingredients when possible. The food menu is designed to complement the beer selection providing satisfying options for guests attending the Thursday night bluegrass sessions or any other visit.

title: Community Jams
venue_description:
Overview

Community Jams is a nonprofit organization that grew from Portland Casual Jams a Meetup.com network of over 4700 local musicians. The organization is dedicated to building community compassion and harmony by connecting musicians of all abilities through live music. Their studio is conveniently located at 2365 SW Cedar Hills Boulevard in Beaverton about a mile from the intersection of Highway 26 and Highway 217.

Mission and Values

The mission of Community Jams is to connect musicians of all abilities in order to build community compassion and harmony by playing live music together. The organization believes in the power of music to bring people together regardless of skill level or background. They maintain a welcoming inclusive environment where everyone from beginners to seasoned professionals can participate and grow.

Regular Jam Sessions

Community Jams hosts multiple weekly jam sessions each designed to serve different needs and skill levels. Monday features the No Request Refused Jam (6-8 PM) and Improv Jam where participants explore improvisation around suggested themes. Thursdays offer Themed Jams (7-9:30 PM) with setlists featuring songs from popular rotating themes. Saturdays include the Newcomer and Explorer Jam (1-4 PM) for those new to jamming or exploring singing or new instruments as well as bi-monthly Blues Jams and Acoustic Jams (4:30-7:30 PM) hosted by Ben. Sunday features the EZ-Lead Slow Jam (1-3 PM) hosted by Bodhi focusing on campfire-style sessions that are easy to follow and join.

Facilities and Equipment

The studio is fully equipped with backline instruments sound systems and everything needed for a successful jam session. Participants can use the provided equipment or bring their own instruments. The space is designed to be comfortable and conducive to musical collaboration with adequate room for both performers and listeners.

Accessibility

Located near major highways the studio is accessible by car with convenient parking. TriMet Bus Line 20 stops across the street connecting Eastside neighborhoods of Portland with Beaverton making the location accessible via public transportation. This commitment to accessibility ensures that musicians from throughout the Portland metro area can participate.

Financial Support and Sustainability

Community Jams operates on a donation-based model with each jam currently costing the organization approximately $24 per person. They encourage participants to contribute $20-$25 per jam or establish recurring donations through PayPal Patreon or Venmo. The organization receives grant support from Pearl Jam's Future Days Fund the Fred W. Fields fund of Oregon Community Foundation and the Marie Lamfrom Charitable Foundation. They are also supported by the Oregon Arts Commission a state agency funded by the State of Oregon.

Community Building

Beyond the music Community Jams uses Discord as a communication platform helping members collaborate on music projects and stay connected between sessions. This online community complements the in-person jams creating lasting connections between musicians. The organization welcomes volunteers interested in helping with marketing website management and social media expanding their community impact.
location: 2365 SW Cedar Hills Blvd Beaverton OR 97005

title: The Goodfoot
venue_description:
Overview

The Goodfoot is a beloved Portland institution that has been featuring live music DJs and dancing in its downstairs lounge since 2001. Located at 2845 SE Stark Street the venue has become known for its eclectic programming spanning soul funk jazz rock comedy and more. In 2026 The Goodfoot celebrated its 25th anniversary cementing its status as one of Portland's most enduring music venues.

Downstairs Lounge

The basement lounge at The Goodfoot feels like a snug grungy speakeasy providing an intimate setting for live music and dancing. The space has hosted countless memorable performances from local and touring acts. The venue's commitment to diverse programming ensures there's always something new and exciting happening whether it's a funk band a rock show or a comedy night.

Music Programming

The Goodfoot features a robust weekly schedule of live music. Regular events include Soul Stew Portland's longest-running DJ dance night delivering deep cuts of funk soul disco and breakbeats on vinyl 45s. The venue hosts bands like Super Secret Band known for their blazing live shows touching on rock dark jazz blues and funk and Jujuba who deliver a funky danceable style of Nigerian Afrobeat. Asher Fulero and Friends appears monthly featuring epic jams with many of Portland's finest musicians joining the keyboard ace for extended improvisation and dance floor-filling performances.

Comedy and Special Events

Monday nights feature Laugh Basement Comedy Showcase hosted by Hewitt Pagenstecher showcasing the funniest comics from the Pacific Northwest and beyond. Sunday evenings offer Drink and Draw events from 7 PM to late hosted by Beth Myrick with rotating guest hosts and variety themes. These events are free and open to all artistic abilities providing supplies for those who don't have their own projects.

Upstairs Bar

The upstairs section of The Goodfoot offers a more traditional bar atmosphere with pool tables and a full food menu. This area provides a contrast to the basement lounge allowing guests to enjoy different experiences within the same venue. The upstairs bar is perfect for those looking for a more relaxed environment before or after catching a show downstairs.

Community and Culture

Over its 25-year history The Goodfoot has become an integral part of Portland's music and arts community. The venue's commitment to supporting local talent while also bringing in touring acts has helped maintain Portland's reputation as a vibrant music city. The Goodfoot's mix of music dance comedy and art creates a unique cultural hub that reflects Portland's creative spirit.
